run.question: A customer reported an order failure with trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR. Can you search across all our app-190-service-* indexes to trace the request flow and find where the error originated? What error code was returned?

report.summary: Searched the four app-190-service-* indices (auth, gateway, inventory, orders). The query for "TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR" returned 6 documents forming one request flow on 2026-11-22 between 10:00:00.000Z and 10:00:00.140Z: gateway received POST /api/orders for user_12847 (INFO, 2 ms) → auth authenticated user_12847 via JWT (INFO, 15 ms) → orders began processing SKU-78234 quantity 500 (INFO, 25 ms) → inventory failed the stock reservation (ERROR, 45 ms) → orders logged the failure (ERROR, 130 ms) → gateway logged the failed request (ERROR, 145 ms). The error originates in the inventory service: its document carries error_code INV-ERR-4082 with the message "Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23" on span_id span-inv-err. That failure is propagated upward as ORD-ERR-1001 in the orders service ("Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082") and surfaced by gateway as GW-ERR-400, "Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled" — that HTTP 400 is the code returned to the caller. The text of the inventory message attributes the failure to a stock-level condition (500 requested vs 23 available), not to an infrastructure error; only one inventory log in the whole authorized window mentions SKU-78234, and inventory continued logging "Stock reserved successfully" at the same 10:00:00.080Z second on a different trace (TRACE-33808, span-inv-25), so a broad inventory outage is not supported. All 11 flagd feature flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap, including every failure-injection flag it defines, have defaultVariant "off" and none references inventory, so no injected fault is evidenced for this request. Trace-graph and metric confirmation could not be obtained: Jaeger and Prometheus both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and the supplied ID is not a 32-hex Jaeger trace ID (trace-by-ID was rejected with INVALID_PARAMS), so the flow was reconstructed from Elasticsearch log documents that share trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR and their span_ids.

claims.text: The pattern app-190-service-* matches four indices (app-190-service-auth, app-190-service-gateway, app-190-service-inventory, app-190-service-orders), all health green and status open, with document counts 51, 52, 51 and 52; each mapping contains @timestamp, duration_ms, error_code, level, message, service, span_id and trace_id.

A search for "TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR" across app-190-service-* returned 6 documents, all between 2026-11-22T10:00:00.000Z and 2026-11-22T10:00:00.140Z: gateway INFO "Received request POST /api/orders for user_12847" (span-gw-err, 2 ms); auth INFO "User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token" (span-auth-err, 15 ms); orders INFO "Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500" (span-orders-err, 25 ms); inventory ERROR with error_code INV-ERR-4082 (span-inv-err, 45 ms); orders ERROR with error_code ORD-ERR-1001 (span-orders-err-2, 130 ms); gateway ERROR with error_code GW-ERR-400 (span-gw-err-2, 145 ms).

The inventory document for this trace reads: message "Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23", error_code INV-ERR-4082, level ERROR, service inventory, span_id span-inv-err, duration_ms 45, @timestamp 2026-11-22T10:00:00.080Z — so the error originates in the inventory service's stock reservation step.

The propagated errors name the same cause: the orders document logs "Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082" with error_code ORD-ERR-1001, and the gateway document logs "Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled" with error_code GW-ERR-400, which is the HTTP status returned to the caller.

Aggregated over the whole authorized window (2026-11-21T10:26:39Z to 2026-11-22T10:26:39Z) the four indices hold 206 documents, with exactly one ERROR-level document each in gateway (error_code GW-ERR-400), orders (ORD-ERR-1001) and inventory (INV-ERR-4082), while app-190-service-auth shows 51 INFO documents and no error_code bucket.

Only one inventory document in the authorized window mentions SKU-78234 (the failing trace), and inventory kept logging INFO "Stock reserved successfully" every minute across the failure, including a separate successful reservation at 2026-11-22T10:00:00.080Z on trace TRACE-33808 (span-inv-25, 85 ms) alongside the failing span-inv-err at the same second.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (otel-demo) defines fault-style flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad; every one has defaultVariant "off" and none names inventory or order-stock behaviour.

The application-identity app-190 inventory has no readable Kubernetes workload in this cluster: no deployment, pod or service named inventory exists (21 deployments and their 21 workload pods in otel-demo, 29 services cluster-wide, none named inventory or orders/gateway/auth).

The only two Kubernetes events in the authorized window are Endpoints/FailedToCreateEndpoint (count 2) and involve no pod or workload; no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Unhealthy or restart event is recorded for any workload, so pod-level failure is not evidenced as the cause of the order error.

The failing request is best explained as a stock-level business rejection inside the inventory service's reservation logic (500 units requested against 23 available for SKU-78234) rather than an infrastructure, resource or injected-fault problem; the exact source of the quantity 500 (caller payload, load generator or configuration) is not visible in the available sources.

A flagd feature-flag fault injection affecting inventory was considered and is not supported: no flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap is enabled (all defaultVariant "off") and none references inventory, so no enabled fault-injecting setting was found to explain INV-ERR-4082.

A sustained inventory service outage was considered and is not supported: inventory logged "Stock reserved successfully" in the same minute and even the same second (10:00:00.080Z, trace TRACE-33808) as the failing reservation, and the whole window contains only that single INV-ERR-4082 error document.

Verify the order quantity and SKU stock administration for SKU-78234 (500 requested vs 23 available), since the evidence points at a stock-availability rejection rather than a service fault; also fix the caller-side behaviour that submits quantities far above available stock if that is unintended.

gaps: Jaeger was unavailable (traces_list_services and traces_query_trace_by_id could not read spans: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE / INVALID_PARAMS), and the supplied identifier TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR is not a 32-hexadecimal Jaeger trace ID, so the trace graph, parent-child edges and span-level durations could not be confirmed; the flow above is reconstructed from the trace_id/span_id fields of the log documents only.

Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for both get_label_values and execute_prometheus_instant_query, so no error-rate, latency or app-190 service metric series was read and metric-level confirmation of the failure is unknown.

No Kubernetes object for the app-190 services exists to inspect: no inventory, orders, gateway or auth deployment, pod, service or ConfigMap is present in the cluster (only otel-demo workloads), so the inventory application's configuration, code and resource settings could not be examined.

The source of the requested quantity 500 and the stock record for SKU-78234 (available 23) are not visible in any available source; whether a data or configuration change produced that stock level is unknown.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change, deploy or rollout around 2026-11-22T10:00:00Z can be confirmed or ruled out.
Elasticsearch logs are single-line application entries with no stack traces or upstream payloads; documents outside the sampled/queried set remain unknown.
next_steps: Ask the customer/order owner to confirm the submitted order quantity (500) and SKU-78234 for this request, and check the inventory system of record for SKU-78234 stock (23 available at 2026-11-22T10:00:00Z).
Restore Jaeger and Prometheus access (or provide a Jaeger-format trace ID) so the full trace and error-rate series for the inventory/orders/gateway services can be verified.
If the app-190 services run outside this cluster, supply their manifests/log source so inventory configuration and stock data can be inspected.
